correctness.rationale: Root forest decomposition yields T prime = v-1+exp(T); solving and substituting proves reciprocal identity (1). Marking root-degree and unique maximum-containing branch gives (2) and (3), whose coefficient comparison establishes distributional identity at every n>=2. The n=1 exception, conditional covariance recurrence, and sharp Hoppe n=3 boundary are explicitly proved. Exact enumeration and integer-recursion checks agree through n=22, but are not substituted for the analytic proof.

value.rationale: An all-n reflection of complete joint distributions conditioned on each possible leaf count is a natural structural relation between a global branching count and the newest vertex depth; it controls every mixed moment and conditional law. It is more than the previously known root-degree/leaf covariance, and fails sharply outside uniform attachment at n=3, giving a meaningful boundary.
